newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Four die as Greek ore carrier sinks off S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Four die as Greek ore carrier sinks off S.Africa.

text.p: Four people died when a Greek-registered ore carrier sank on Saturday off South Africa's Indian Ocean coast, sea rescue and port officials said.

The 74,278 tonne carrier, named the Iollos Victor, sank at about 0630 GMT on Saturday, 107 nautical miles south of Cape St Francis near the Indian Ocean port city of Port Elizabeth, assistant port captain Brian Phipps told Reuters.
"We have picked up four bodies from the sea. There are also 21 survivors who have also been picked up by rescue helicopters and a fishing trawler," he said.
A crew of 25 had been on board the iron ore carrier when it started taking in water in its forward hatches before sinking, Phipps added.
"The situation was worsened by bad weather conditions around where she (the carrier) sank. There are big swells of about six metres and it is raining hard there," he said.
Sixteen of the 21 surviving seamen had been taken aboard a Japanese fishing trawler which had also responded to the crew's distress call.
Phipps said a helicopter shuttle service was transporting the survivors, some suffering from hypothermia, to hospital. Four were in critical condition.
A Port Elizabeth ambulance spokesman, Lungile Yekela, said the carrier had been on its way from the Philippines to Port Elizabeth.
